content: Partial-failure handling in bulk import: Postgres transactions are atomic by default (all-or-nothing), which is wrong for 'import 500 rows, 3 are bad' scenarios since it would roll back 497 good rows. Recommended pattern: validate/stage rows first (in-memory or a staging table) before touching production tables, only commit rows that pass validation, and surface failed rows back to the user for correction rather than committing partial writes silently. ON CONFLICT (upsert) needs explicit guard conditions to avoid clobbering concurrent updates.
